### Verifiable takeaways from the table
- Net debt inflows peak at **85.9** in **2021** and are lowest at **45.9** in **2016**.
- Long-term inflows peak at **78.2** in **2020** and are lowest at **44.0** in **2022**.
- Official creditors exceed private creditors in every year except **2021**, when private creditors are **31.6** versus official creditors at **37.2**—official still remain larger; the closest parity is **2017** and **2018** where private creditors are **31.9** and official creditors are **31.1**/**39.1**.
- Within official creditors, **multilateral creditors** are larger than **bilateral creditors** in every year except **2018**.
- **World Bank** inflows rise from **7.2** in 2015 to a peak of **18.3** in 2024, then decline to **14.8** in 2025.
- **IMF** inflows spike sharply in **2020** to **15.2**, then fall to **3.2** in 2021 and later rise to **6.9** in 2024 before easing to **5.7** in 2025.
- **Private creditors** fall to a low of **4.5** in **2022**, then recover to **23.9** in **2025**.
- **Bonds** are negative in **2022** (**−2.0**) and **2023** (**−0.3**), then turn positive again in **2024** and **2025**.
- **Short-term** inflows are negative in **2016** (**−0.4**), **2018** (**−4.1**), **2020** (**−0.7**), and **2023** (**−11.0**), with the largest positive value of **19.2** in **2017**.
- In memorandum items, **Long-term PPG** is larger than **Long-term PNG** in every year.
- **Long-term PNG** turns negative only in **2024** (**−0.4**).

**Sources:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database; International Monetary Fund; Bank for International Settlements.

**Note:** IBRD = International Bank for Reconstruction and Development; IDA = International Development Association; IMF = International Monetary Fund; PNG = private nonguaranteed; PPG = public and publicly guaranteed.
